answer_text:
Let \(w=z-2\). For \(|w|<1\), the geometric series gives

\[
\frac{1}{1-w}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} w^n.
\]

Integrating term-by-term from \(0\) to \(w\),

\[
\int_0^w \frac{1}{1-t}\,dt
= \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{w^{n+1}}{n+1}.
\]

The left side is

\[
-\ln(1-w),
\]

and the right side is

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{w^n}{n}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{w^n}{n}=-\ln(1-w).
\]

Substituting \(w=z-2\),

\[
h(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(z-2)^n}{n}
=-\ln\bigl(1-(z-2)\bigr)
=-\ln(3-z).
\]

This holds on the disk of convergence \(|z-2|<1\), with the branch of \(\ln\) chosen so that \(\ln 1=0\).

\[
\boxed{h(z)=-\ln(3-z)}
\]
